descriptionChirho: A feminine noun denoting a state of quietness, tranquility, ease, or carefree prosperity, ranging from positive peace to negative complacency depending on context. Used positively of peaceful security in Ps 122:7 and the value of quiet contentment in Prov 17:1. Used negatively of complacent ease that destroys fools (Prov 1:32), the idle luxury of Sodom (Ezek 16:49), and the false security in which Jeremiah's audience refused to listen (Jer 22:21). In Daniel, describes the deceptive peace by which the willful king conquers (Dan 8:25; 11:21, 24). Multilingual glosses consistently show Arabic salaam/tuma'nina, Hindi shaanti/nishchintata, Korean pyeongan, Spanish tranquilidad/prosperidad, confirming a unified semantic range of untroubled ease.
